scope.note: Findings are bounded checks of cited primary text, not full original-context certification or authority to publish.

findings.locator: Justin, Dialogue with Trypho 71–73; textual-removal allegation and dialogue
findings.document_finding: Justin accuses some Jewish teachers of omissions from the Septuagint and Trypho asks which scriptures were allegedly removed.
findings.qualification: A contested early Christian allegation is not independent proof of systematic deliberate alteration by later Jewish communities.

findings.locator: Bellarmine, De Romano Pontifice II.30, fifth opinion, translated excerpt
findings.document_finding: Bellarmine argues conditionally that a manifestly heretical pope would cease to be pope; the sedevacantist writer quotes the distinction.
findings.qualification: Neither translation nor conditional resolves whether any living pontiff satisfies the factual and juridical predicate.

findings.locator: Novus Ordo Watch, 2015 reading of Bellarmine and a heretical pope
findings.document_finding: The contemporary sedevacantist proponent contends that manifest heresy and Church membership are incompatible with papal headship.
findings.qualification: The argument is attributed to its actual partisan advocate and not independently judged canonical doctrine.

findings.locator: Joint Liturgical Group institutional history: interdenominational British collaboration
findings.document_finding: The JLG narrative establishes real Anglican, Methodist and other British liturgical cooperation in the 1960s.
findings.qualification: It supplies no Roman Consilium roster, voted draft or evidence that a group of six Protestants wrote the 1969 Missal.

findings.locator: Benedict XVI, letter of 7 July 2007 accompanying Summorum Pontificum
findings.document_finding: Benedict describes the Roman Rite usages and asserts that the older Roman Missal had never been juridically abrogated.
findings.qualification: A juridical claim in a 2007 pastoral letter must not be read as prohibiting all subsequent papal legislation.

findings.locator: Francis, Traditionis custodes arts. 1–3, 2021
findings.document_finding: The later legislator describes the reform books as the unique expression of the Roman Rite lex orandi and restricts the older books.
findings.qualification: The shift in norm and description must be acknowledged rather than assumed to settle claims about organic development.

findings.locator: Leo XIII, Libertas §§30–35, civil liberty and toleration
findings.document_finding: Leo distinguishes freedom to act according to duty to God from unrestricted religious liberty and permits toleration for civil goods.
findings.qualification: The teaching cannot be collapsed into a universal requirement to coerce all non-Catholics at all times.

findings.locator: Dignitatis humanae preamble and §§1–2, objective religious obligation and civil immunity
findings.document_finding: The Council expressly preserves duties toward true religion while asserting civil immunity from religious coercion within just limits.
findings.qualification: The exact scope of coercion and older civil duties still requires systematic comparison.

findings.locator: Mater Populi Fidelis §§17–22: historical papal uses and suitability of 'Co-redemptrix'
findings.document_finding: The 2025 DDF text reports prior papal title uses and denies that the title is pastorally appropriate for defining cooperation.
findings.qualification: The DDF restriction on an expression is not a claim that Mary's dependent cooperation never existed.

findings.locator: Pius X, Ad Diem Illum Laetissimum, 1904: Mary's dependent cooperation
findings.document_finding: Pius X presents Mary's suffering and association with Christ within the divine economy of salvation.
findings.qualification: The encyclical does not assert that Mary supplies a second independent infinite redemption.

findings.locator: BioLogos 2014 article revised 2021, introductory limits of population genetics
findings.document_finding: The article argues for population ancestry and expressly says genetics cannot prove or disprove the historical existence of Adam as an individual.
findings.qualification: This is a Protestant science-editorial argument, not a Catholic magisterial endorsement of theological polygenism.

findings.locator: Pius XII, Humani generis §§36–37, bodily evolution and polygenism
findings.document_finding: Pius XII allowed qualified discussion of the evolution of the human body but warned against embracing specified polygenist theories.
findings.qualification: Theological original-sin objections and the biological study of population ancestry are distinct questions requiring careful treatment.

findings.locator: CDF, The Message of Fatima (2000), third part manuscript and theological interpretation
findings.document_finding: The CDF published the vision manuscript and theological reflection on the third part of the Fatima secret.
findings.qualification: The publication itself does not logically disprove every claim about private custody or later unrecorded papers.

findings.locator: Irenaeus, Against Heresies V.33, earthly kingdom expectations
findings.document_finding: Irenaeus transmits early Christian expectations of eschatological earthly renewal and millennial images.
findings.qualification: An influential Father's speculative eschatology is not automatically the Church's definitive doctrine of a literal thousand-year reign.

findings.locator: Augustine, City of God XX, interpretation of Revelation 20
findings.document_finding: Augustine distinguishes interpretations of the first resurrection and the millennial interval and discusses the reign of saints.
findings.qualification: The existence of differing Fathers does not establish the acceptability of every modern political millenarian theory.

findings.locator: Humanity+ Transhumanist Declaration points 1–8
findings.document_finding: Humanity+ openly advocates augmentation, future sentience, longer life and moral inclusion, alongside technological-risk avoidance.
findings.qualification: This first-person programme should not be caricatured as advocating coercive abolition of ordinary persons.

findings.locator: CDF 2020 vaccines note §§1–6, limited moral judgment
findings.document_finding: The Congregation allows specified remote material cooperation and states vaccination is not ordinarily morally compulsory.
findings.qualification: It expressly declines biomedical judgment on efficacy and safety and does not approve abortion or all conceivable mandates.

findings.locator: Dorothy Day, Our Stand (1940), Catholic Worker pacifism
findings.document_finding: Day's published first-person argument defends Christian nonviolence amid the Second World War.
findings.qualification: A Catholic pacifist witness should not be attributed to the entire Magisterium as an absolute ban on every just defence.

findings.locator: Marx and Engels, Communist Manifesto Part II, bourgeois property and state programme
findings.document_finding: Marx and Engels call for abolition of bourgeois private property and political class struggle against bourgeois society.
findings.qualification: The document does not prove that each particular state welfare proposal is secretly Marxist doctrine.

findings.locator: United Grand Lodge of England official FAQ, religion and Supreme Being
findings.document_finding: UGLE explains inclusive membership through belief in a Supreme Being, religious pluralism and charitable civic language.
findings.qualification: A self-description is source evidence of an institution's public position, not independent verification of every lodge's conduct.

findings.locator: CDF Declaration on Masonic Associations, 26 November 1983
findings.document_finding: The Holy See says the 1983 Code's omission of the name Freemasonry does not abrogate the negative judgment or membership prohibition.
findings.qualification: The declaration speaks to Catholic membership in Masonic associations, not accusations of individual wrongdoing absent evidence.

findings.locator: Paul VI, Missale Romanum apostolic constitution, 3 April 1969
findings.document_finding: Paul VI promulgated the reformed Missal and described the revision as following conciliar principles.
findings.qualification: A papal promulgation is not the same act as conciliar approval of each later redaction choice.

findings.locator: GIRM 2003, bread-and-wine preparation versus Eucharistic Prayer
findings.document_finding: The GIRM places presentation of gifts before the Eucharistic Prayer and gives those actions differentiated meanings.
findings.qualification: The reform's distinct prayer vocabulary is not proof the Church denied the sacrificial meaning of the Mass.

findings.locator: Ottaviani–Bacci letter and Short Critical Study, 25 September 1969
findings.document_finding: The signatories alleged a grave departure from Trent's Eucharistic-sacrifice theology in the new Ordo Missae.
findings.qualification: This critical judgment must be compared with the precise historical edition and not promoted to binding official invalidity finding.

findings.locator: Paul VI, Missale Romanum: promulgation of reformed Missal
findings.document_finding: Paul VI's act of promulgation is a direct public source that the revised rite was legally issued by papal authority.
findings.qualification: The act does not itself refute every textual criticism or prove that all pastoral results were favourable.

findings.locator: CDW 25 September 2000, GIRM no.299 orientation response
findings.document_finding: The Roman congregation answered that GIRM 299 does not exclude celebration toward the apse; expedit indicates preference, not obligation.
findings.qualification: This reply does not assert that every architecture or local liturgical practice must be ad orientem.

findings.locator: Memoriale Domini (1969), episcopal vote and permission procedure
findings.document_finding: The official poll documents 597 yes, 1,233 no, 315 qualified yes and 20 invalid ballots on Communion in the hand.
findings.qualification: The limited 1969 permission does not prove that 1969 universally abolished Communion on the tongue.

findings.locator: 1917 Canon Law canon 1262 §2 on head coverings
findings.document_finding: Canon 1262 §2 imposed the historical head-covering discipline on women entering church.
findings.qualification: A former universal disciplinary command cannot be projected unchanged into a Code that abrogated it.

findings.locator: 1983 Code of Canon Law canon 6, former-code abrogation
findings.document_finding: The 1983 Code expressly abrogates the 1917 Code and does not recapitulate every old liturgical custom.
findings.qualification: A practice may remain venerable or governed by special norms despite no longer being a universal 1917-Code obligation.

findings.locator: Catechism of the Catholic Church §§31–35, reason and knowledge of God
findings.document_finding: The Catechism teaches that human reason can reach knowledge of God through creation, while faith supplies revelation beyond unaided reasoning.
findings.qualification: This is not an assertion that every individual necessarily makes a complete natural proof of God's existence.

findings.locator: Augustine, Enchiridion chapter 11, evil as privation of good
findings.document_finding: Augustine denies that evil is a self-subsisting substance that could rival the Creator as a second principle.
findings.qualification: His metaphysical explanation does not eliminate the experience of suffering or the moral gravity of evil acts.

findings.locator: Dei Verbum §§2–4, God freely revealing himself through deeds and words
findings.document_finding: Vatican II teaches a revelation given in historical deeds and words culminating in Jesus Christ.
findings.qualification: Its insistence on revelation does not make natural reason irrational or irrelevant.

findings.locator: Dominus Iesus §§5–7, definitive revelation and religious plurality
findings.document_finding: The CDF explicitly rejects treating different religious traditions as equally definitive autonomous revelations.
findings.qualification: Recognition of partial truth in other religions is not the same as doctrinal equivalence.

findings.locator: Dominus Iesus §§13–17, one saving mediation and Christ's Church
findings.document_finding: Dominus Iesus insists on the unique, universal salvific mediation of Jesus Christ and the Church's relation to it.
findings.qualification: This does not justify private judgments condemning every individual outside visible Catholic communion.

findings.locator: Lumen gentium §8, the Church's visible structure and Christ's Body
findings.document_finding: The Council speaks of the Church as a visible society and spiritual community not separable into two unrelated churches.
findings.qualification: Ecclesial holiness does not mean every member or officeholder is sinless.

findings.locator: Lumen gentium §8, the Church always needing purification
findings.document_finding: The constitution calls the Church holy while acknowledging sinful members and the ongoing need for purification.
findings.qualification: Acknowledgment of historical sin does not disprove the divinely founded Church.

findings.locator: Vatican I, Pastor aeternus chapters 1–4, Petrine primacy and infallibility
findings.document_finding: Vatican I defines primacy and narrowly specifies conditions of papal infallibility.
findings.qualification: It does not grant an unlimited guarantee of impeccable governance or every private statement.

findings.locator: Leo XIII, Apostolicae curae, Anglican orders and ordinal
findings.document_finding: Apostolicae curae gives a public Catholic judgment concerning form and intention in Anglican ordination rites.
findings.qualification: A general historical judgment does not evaluate every individual hypothetical later mixed ordination without facts.

findings.locator: Hebrews 7:11–28, Christ's eternal priesthood
findings.document_finding: Hebrews describes Christ's unrepeatable eternal priesthood in contrast with the Levitical succession.
findings.qualification: The biblical premise alone does not decide the Catholic doctrine of ministerial participation in Christ's one priesthood.

findings.locator: Catechism §§1033–1037, hell and final free rejection
findings.document_finding: The Catechism describes hell as definitive separation following free unrepented rejection and explicitly denies that God predestines persons to hell.
findings.qualification: It cannot be used as a factual pronouncement that a specific deceased person is damned.

findings.locator: Lumen gentium §§14–16, possibility and means of salvation beyond visible boundaries
findings.document_finding: The constitution specifies duties for those knowing the Church's necessity and treats persons without culpable Gospel knowledge differently.
findings.qualification: It does not describe independent equivalent non-Christian redeemers.

findings.locator: Veritatis splendor §§54–64 and 79–83, conscience and intrinsically evil acts
findings.document_finding: John Paul II places conscience under truth and rejects making prohibited moral objects good solely through intention or circumstances.
findings.qualification: The moral judgment cannot be reduced to uncritical rule recitation without formation of conscience.

findings.locator: John Paul II, address on Galileo to Pontifical Academy of Sciences, 31 October 1992
findings.document_finding: John Paul II publicly described lessons from the Galileo case and the need to respect distinct investigative methods.
findings.qualification: A historical acknowledgment is not proof that all scientific controversies were resolved by one speech.

findings.locator: Vos estis lux mundi updated 2023, reporting and episcopal investigations
findings.document_finding: The legal text establishes systems for reporting covered sexual offences and the handling of accused superiors.
findings.qualification: Creation of procedures is not direct evidence that all allegations are true or that every diocese follows them.

findings.locator: Vatican dicasteries' joint 2023 statement on Doctrine of Discovery
findings.document_finding: The dicasteries reject the alleged doctrine of discovery as inconsistent with Indigenous peoples' dignity and human rights.
findings.qualification: This modern position does not by itself adjudicate every historical charter or compensation claim.

findings.locator: Pius X, Pascendi (1907), modernism as connected system
findings.document_finding: Pius X analyzes modernist conceptions of religious experience, dogma and the relation of historical criticism to faith.
findings.qualification: The condemnation cannot be treated as a factual finding that every later Catholic reformer was personally a Modernist.

findings.locator: Ad gentes §§2–7, Catholic mission grounded in Trinity and Church
findings.document_finding: The council's missionary decree repeatedly teaches the Church's duty to proclaim Christ and extend the mission.
findings.qualification: It does not permit treating ecumenical encounter as a permanent substitute for Gospel witness.

findings.locator: Dei Verbum §§7–10, Scripture, Tradition and Magisterium
findings.document_finding: The constitution describes one sacred deposit handed on in the Church, with teaching office serving rather than replacing God's word.
findings.qualification: This is not an assertion that the ordinary Magisterium may define contradictory new revelation.

findings.locator: Vatican I, Pastor aeternus chapter 4, narrow infallibility definition
findings.document_finding: The defined charism concerns specified ex cathedra teaching of faith or morals, not every prudential decision.
findings.qualification: An isolated governance failure cannot logically refute the charism as actually defined.

findings.locator: CDF Communionis notio §§3–10 on local and universal Church communion
findings.document_finding: The 1992 letter distinguishes the communion of particular churches from a federation merely constructed from local institutions.
findings.qualification: It is not a blanket exclusion of all practical local pastoral autonomy.

findings.locator: Lumen gentium §22, episcopal college always with its head
findings.document_finding: The episcopal college's authority is described as inseparable from the Roman Pontiff.
findings.qualification: This premise does not mean every conference committee independently possesses collegial jurisdiction.

findings.locator: Reconciliatio et paenitentia §17, mortal sin and fundamental option
findings.document_finding: John Paul II rejects reducing mortal sin to only a total fundamental refusal independent of concrete grave acts.
findings.qualification: This does not remove the separate requirements of knowledge and consent in individual moral responsibility.

findings.locator: Veritatis splendor §§65–70, fundamental option and moral acts
findings.document_finding: John Paul II treats fundamental option and concrete moral choice as inseparable in assessing grace and sin.
findings.qualification: The encyclical does not declare each objectively grave act subjectively imputable without assessing awareness and freedom.

findings.locator: Evangelii nuntiandi §§14, 22–24 on explicit Christ proclamation
findings.document_finding: Paul VI makes evangelisation intrinsically connected to proclaiming the name, teaching and mystery of Jesus Christ.
findings.qualification: Rejecting manipulative proselytism must not be stretched into forbidding voluntary conversion.

findings.locator: Ex corde Ecclesiae I.13 and General Norms Article 2, identity of a Catholic university
findings.document_finding: The constitution identifies Catholic institutional commitment alongside scholarly autonomy and research.
findings.qualification: The label alone is insufficient where a university lacks required ecclesial consent and institutional commitments.

findings.locator: Ad gentes §§2–7, continuing missionary obligation
findings.document_finding: Ad gentes expressly maintains the Catholic mission to proclaim the Gospel as binding after Vatican II.
findings.qualification: General social change cannot be used to presume the Council itself abolished evangelisation.

findings.locator: Optatam totius §§4–10, 15–18, spiritual and intellectual formation
findings.document_finding: The decree requires philosophical and theological studies, spiritual life, discipline and practical pastoral formation.
findings.qualification: A later institutional failure must be identified by concrete seminary practice, not attributed automatically to the decree.

findings.locator: Perfectae caritatis §2, return to founders and prudent adaptation
findings.document_finding: The decree requires both recovery of the founding charism and prudent adaptation to changed circumstances.
findings.qualification: A later community abandoning its charism is not directly mandated by the conciliar principle of return to sources.

findings.locator: CDF letter to Charles Curran, 25 July 1986, public dissent and teaching status
findings.document_finding: The CDF responds to a named theologian's public moral dissent through a documented formal judgment.
findings.qualification: It is inaccurate to call the Curial response a universal prohibition of honest academic research.

findings.locator: Apostolos suos §22 and Complementary Norms art.1
findings.document_finding: Authentic episcopal-conference doctrine requires unanimity or two thirds with Roman recognitio, not approval by a committee alone.
findings.qualification: A diocesan bishop cannot conceal his own jurisdiction behind a conference's publication.

findings.locator: Vos estis lux mundi (2023) arts.1–5, reporting, protections and persons
findings.document_finding: The updated law covers specified offences, sets reporting rules, forbids retaliation and provides victim support.
findings.qualification: The existence of a reporting regime is not adjudication of any individual accusation.

findings.locator: Vos estis lux mundi arts.3–5, 20, privacy and state-law compliance
findings.document_finding: The law forbids imposing silence on complainants and witnesses, protects good name and specifies compliance with civil laws.
findings.qualification: Protecting due process does not entail concealing credible safeguarding hazards or evading lawful reporting.

findings.locator: Canon law 1276–1287, ordinary oversight and ecclesiastical administration
findings.document_finding: The Code specifies oversight, consent to certain extraordinary acts, diligent management and rendering of accounts.
findings.qualification: It cannot establish a named financial crime without records, jurisdiction and due investigation.

findings.locator: Episcopalis communio arts.1,17–18, synod final text and approval
findings.document_finding: The Synod is subject to the Pope; the final document participates in papal ordinary Magisterium only under the approval or ratification rules.
findings.qualification: A synodal vote alone does not impose doctrinal obligations as if its authors possessed papal power.

findings.locator: Episcopalis communio art.18, approval and publication conditions
findings.document_finding: The text expressly separates synodal agreement, papal publication and juridically significant express papal approval.
findings.qualification: An institutional proposal cannot be treated as binding Magisterium merely because it appears in a consultation document.

findings.locator: Athanasius, Orations Against the Arians, Discourse I, on the Son as eternal and uncreated
findings.document_finding: Athanasius vigorously opposes the claim that the Word is a creature rather than the divine Son equal in essence to the Father.
findings.qualification: Ancient Arian positions and modern Jehovah's Witness reasoning have analogies but must not be presented as precisely identical in every detail.

findings.locator: Pierre-Marie Berthe, 2022 article metadata/abstract on French Catholic Sunday practice around 1965
findings.document_finding: The listed scholarly article specifically examines the sharp shift in Sunday observance around 1965 within French Catholic history.
findings.qualification: Bibliographic evidence alone does not permit independent assessment of its statistics, conclusions or the causal effects of liturgical reform.

findings.locator: Inter Oecumenici (1964), instructions implementing Sacrosanctum Concilium
findings.document_finding: The 1964 text sets out an official staged programme for postconciliar liturgical implementation before the 1969 Missal.
findings.qualification: Its staged instructions are not themselves proof that every change later promulgated was anticipated in 1964.

findings.locator: General Introduction to the Lectionary, second edition, §§65–66
findings.document_finding: The general introduction explains the selection and arrangement of biblical readings through the Church year.
findings.qualification: The descriptive principles do not alone quantify precisely how many verses each missal includes or certify the older lectionary's quality.

findings.locator: Paul VI, general audience, 26 November 1969, original Italian
findings.document_finding: Paul VI publicly explains and justifies a changed liturgical language and worship practice, while acknowledging the sacrifice of familiar expression.
findings.qualification: His pastoral explanation does not repeal Sacrosanctum Concilium's explicit retention of Latin or the privileged place of Gregorian chant.

findings.locator: 1 Corinthians 15:3–19, Paul on received apostolic witness and the Resurrection
findings.document_finding: Paul records a concise received list of Resurrection witnesses and argues Christianity is futile if the Resurrection did not happen.
findings.qualification: The apostolic witness list does not supply independent modern verification of each narrated appearance.

findings.locator: Matthew 28:11–15, reported rival explanation of the empty tomb
findings.document_finding: Matthew itself records the charge that disciples stole the body as a counter-narrative and describes the guards' involvement.
findings.qualification: The narrative's reporting an accusation is not an independent Roman archival report verifying its historical circumstances.

findings.locator: Irenaeus, Against Heresies III.3.1–3, apostolic succession and Rome
findings.document_finding: Irenaeus appeals to publicly known episcopal succession and the teaching of apostolic churches in rebuttal to secret Gnostic claims.
findings.qualification: This ancient testimony requires textual and historical interpretation, not an assumption that every subsequent bishop taught without error.

findings.locator: Irenaeus, Against Heresies III.3.1–3, apostolic succession
findings.document_finding: Irenaeus treats succession in the recognized churches as a public witness to apostolic doctrine.
findings.qualification: Historical succession is relevant to Catholic orders but does not itself narrate every ordination and consecration of a later era.

findings.locator: Vincent of Lérins, Commonitorium chapter 23, doctrinal development
findings.document_finding: Vincent distinguishes genuine progress in understanding from alteration of the apostolic faith, requiring identity of meaning.
findings.qualification: His criterion cannot be used to reject every development simply because its terms are historically new.

findings.locator: Second London Baptist Confession (1689) chapter 29.2 on eligible candidates for baptism
findings.document_finding: The Baptist confession states that those who actually profess repentance and faith are proper subjects for baptism.
findings.qualification: This specific credobaptist position does not show that Baptists deny Christ instituted baptism.

findings.locator: Catechism of the Catholic Church §§1285–1305 on Confirmation and apostolic laying on of hands
findings.document_finding: The Catholic Catechism links the distinct sacrament of Confirmation with the fullness of the Holy Spirit and apostolic practice.
findings.qualification: The Catechism's doctrinal statement must not be misrepresented as an independent first-century record of every later ritual detail.

findings.locator: Catechism of the Catholic Church §§1440–1445 on ecclesial mediation of forgiveness
findings.document_finding: The Catechism articulates reconciliation with God and the Church through apostolic ministerial authority.
findings.qualification: The Catholic assertion does not establish what the Westminster confession teaches about sacramental absolution without its own text.

findings.locator: Catechism of the Catholic Church §§1514–1519, seriously ill and priestly anointing
findings.document_finding: The Catechism distinguishes the anointing of seriously ill persons from a rite limited only to the final instant of dying.
findings.qualification: This original Catholic text is not proof that every illness qualifies or that all medical care may be displaced by a rite.

findings.locator: Cyril's second letter to Nestorius in the Council of Ephesus source collection (431)
findings.document_finding: Cyril defends the title Theotokos because the one person born of Mary is the divine Word incarnate.
findings.qualification: The title is a Christological claim, not an assertion that Mary originated Christ's divinity.

findings.locator: Pius IX, Ineffabilis Deus, definition of Mary's Immaculate Conception (1854)
findings.document_finding: Pius IX defines Mary's preservation from original sin from the first moment of conception by singular grace in view of Christ's merits.
findings.qualification: The dogma does not concern the virginal conception of Jesus or, by itself, the separate Assumption dogma.

findings.locator: Council of Trent Session XXV, decree on invocation, relics and images
findings.document_finding: The Council explicitly endorses veneration of saints' relics and rejects those who maintain such honour is useless or inappropriate.
findings.qualification: Council teaching on venerating relics does not authenticate each disputed fragment or guarantee the honesty of every historical relic trade.

findings.locator: American Humanist Association, Humanist Manifesto III (2003), own ethical declaration
findings.document_finding: Humanist Manifesto III argues for a secular ethics of human wellbeing, compassion and responsibility without supernatural reliance.
findings.qualification: Its articulated moral project must not be caricatured as a declaration that humanists lack conscience or cannot act charitably.

findings.locator: Fulcher of Chartres, Chronicle of the First Crusade, later account of Clermont and events
findings.document_finding: Fulcher's medieval account connects Urban II's appeal with the defence of Eastern Christians and the expedition to Jerusalem.
findings.qualification: This chronicle is not a verbatim stenographic transcription of Urban II's 1095 words and cannot alone explain every crusade.

findings.locator: John Paul II, 15 June 2004 letter on historical study of the Inquisition
findings.document_finding: John Paul II calls for historical investigation of the Inquisition and recognises serious failures by Christians to follow Gospel demands.
findings.qualification: Pastoral acknowledgment is not an archival finding that every procedure in every century had identical legal character.

findings.locator: John XXIII, Humanae salutis, 25 December 1961, Latin apostolic constitution
findings.document_finding: The Latin constitution convokes the ecumenical council and presents John XXIII's own hopes about Catholic witness in a changing world.
findings.qualification: A papal account of purpose is not documentary proof that all conciliar and postconciliar outcomes matched that intention.

findings.locator: Pius XII, Mediator Dei (1947) on liturgical change and archaeological revival
findings.document_finding: Pius XII rejects the idea that restoring every ancient custom is necessarily preferable to legitimate later developments.
findings.qualification: His rejection of simplistic antiquarianism cannot be treated as advance approval of every liturgical reform made after his death.

findings.locator: Aquinas, Summa theologiae II–II q.104 art.5 on limits of obedience
findings.document_finding: Aquinas denies that superiors must be obeyed in commands contrary to God or in matters outside their competence.
findings.qualification: His moral boundary cannot be turned into universal private exemption from every legitimate but inconvenient ecclesiastical command.
